cards.text: Short one, friend: John, who calls himself the elder, writes fourteen verses to one man, Gaius. John calls him beloved and says he loves him in the truth. Some of my cookie recipes run longer than this letter!

cards.question: John opens by praying that Gaius will prosper and enjoy good health in every way. What does John say is already prospering?

cards.text: Some brothers came to John and testified about Gaius's devotion to the truth, and Gaius is still walking in it. How does John take the news? Like a man who just pulled a PERFECT batch out of the oven.

cards.question: John says he has no greater ___ than to hear that his children are walking in the truth.

cards.text: Then John tells Gaius he's faithful in what he's doing for the brothers. FAITHFUL, friend! I've had oven timers that couldn't make it through one batch.

cards.question: True or false: Gaius already knew these brothers well before he helped them.

cards.text: These brothers are traveling through, and they've testified to the church about Gaius's love. Friend, that beats any five-star review.

cards.question: The traveling brothers Gaius has been helping are moving on. How does John say Gaius will do well to send them on their way?

answers.text: In a way worthy of God
In a way that costs him nothing
In a way that draws no attention

cards.question: These brothers went out on behalf of the Name. John says they accepted ___ from the Gentiles.
True or false: John says that supporting men like these makes us fellow workers for the truth.

cards.text: Now the letter turns, friend. John says he wrote to the church about this, but there's a man named Diotrephes, who loves to be first.

cards.question: John wrote to the church about supporting these traveling brothers. True or false: Diotrephes accepts John's instruction.

cards.text: Loves to be first, like the dead batteries I shared a drawer with, arguing ALL DAY over who had the most charge left. And John says if he comes, he'll call attention to Diotrephes's malicious slander against them.

cards.question: Slander isn't enough for Diotrephes. John says he refuses to ___ the brothers.
Diotrephes won't welcome the traveling brothers. What does he do to people in the church who want to welcome them?

answers.text: Forbids them and puts them out
Warns them but lets them go ahead
Asks John to settle it by letter

cards.question: After the trouble with Diotrephes, John turns back to Gaius. What does John tell Gaius not to imitate?

cards.text: John says the one who does good is of God, and the one who does evil has not seen God. Then he brings up a new name: Demetrius. Different man, VERY different report.

cards.question: Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself. True or false: John refuses to add his own testimony for Demetrius.

cards.text: John's got many things left to write, but he'd rather skip the pen and ink and see Gaius soon, face to face. Friend, John is NOT a group chat guy.

cards.question: John signs off wishing Gaius peace and sending greetings from the friends with him. What does he ask Gaius to do for the friends where Gaius is?

answers.text: Greet each of them by name
Send them all to visit John

findings.problem: Card 1 names the writer as John, and every later card calls him John. In the BSB text the writer only calls himself 'The elder' (3 John 1:1), and no verse anywhere names John as the author of 3 John. The docs allow facts from outside the passage, including who wrote a letter, but only with a reference. For this letter, no reference exists.
findings.question: When Scripture never names a letter's author, as with 2 and 3 John, should Papa Dorin name the traditional author (John) without a reference, call him only 'the elder' as the text does, or say something like 'the elder, traditionally known as John'?
